scenes.event: Ethan and his colleagues take a coffee break to discuss the recent management changes and their impact on the team.
scenes.description: The break room is a small, quiet space with a coffee machine, a few tables, and a microwave. Ethan sits at a table, sipping his coffee slowly, while his colleagues Tiffany and Mike join him, trying to ease the tension in the air.

characters.name: Ethan
characters.description: 31-year-old salesperson at a mid-sized company, feeling anxious and contemplative due to recent management changes and pressure to improve sales.; Male / Employee, 31 years old; Occupation: Salesperson; Personality: Anxious, Resilient, Contemplative, Determined; Values: Stability, Self-worth, Independence; Interests: Career Development, Problem Solving, Self-reflection; Experiences: Workplace Instability, Performance Pressure, Colleague Support, Considering Career Transition, Management Changes

characters.name: Mike
characters.description: Experienced sales manager who is pragmatic and focused on results, often serving as a voice of reason for the team; Male; Age: 42; Occupation: Sales Manager; Personality: Calm, Analytical, Diplomatic; Values: Teamwork, Integrity, Efficiency; Interests: Reading business strategy books, Playing chess online; Experiences: Led a sales team through a major corporate restructuring, Implemented a data-driven sales approach that increased revenue by 20%

actions.dialogue: Hey Ethan, I know things have been tough lately, but you're doing a great job. Don't let Tao's words get to you.
Thanks, Tiffany. I just can't shake the feeling that this new management will be harder on us. I'm thinking about a change, but I don't want to admit it yet.
I've seen this before, Ethan. Management changes can be rocky, but it's also a chance to reset. What's your plan if you stay? Because we need to hit those numbers.
I want to prove that I'm capable and that I can handle the pressure. But if this doesn't work out, I need to find something more stable for my future.
You're not alone in this. We can help each other out. Just don't lose sight of what you're worth.
Let's focus on the next quarter's goals. If we can deliver, maybe the new management will see the value in keeping people like us.

scenes.plot: Ethan struggles with the uncertainty of his job after a management shake-up. His colleagues Tiffany and Mike offer support and perspective, helping him consider his options while reinforcing his determination to find stability and prove his self-worth.
scenes.social_purpose: To explore Ethan's internal conflict and values through a supportive and goal-oriented conversation with colleagues.

chunk.text: Ethan sat at the table, his coffee cooling as he listened to Tiffany and Mike. He appreciated their support, but the weight of his decision pressed down on him. He knew he had to act soon, but the thought of leaving the only job he'd ever known made him hesitate.
